walkthroughs.body_html:
Area of Study 5: Conventions of Pop — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area of Study 5: Conventions of Pop brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area of Study 5: Conventions of Pop.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many crotchets equal a semibreve?
A dot after a note adds?
options: A quarter of its value
A half of its value
A full extra
A double value

mcqs.q: What is characteristic of Baroque music?
options: Simple melodies with piano accompaniment.
Continuous bass line, ornamentation, terraced dynamics, and counterpoint.
Heavy use of electric guitars.
Three notes played at once.
Vibrato on a single note.
Three notes played at once.
A piece six bars long.

mcqs.q: What does the time signature 6/8 indicate?
options: Six beats per bar, all equal in stress.
A piece six bars long.
Heavy use of electric guitars.
Two beats per bar, each beat divided into three (compound duple).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Crotchet (quarter note)”?
options: Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Symbol indicating silence for a specific duration, mirroring note values.
Filled head with single tail/flag; lasts half a beat in 4/4.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Note value”?
options: Symbol indicating silence for a specific duration, mirroring note values.
Filled head with single tail/flag; lasts half a beat in 4/4.
Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Semibreve (whole note)”?
options: Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.
Dot after note increases its duration by half (e.g., dotted crotchet = 1.5 beats).
Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.
Symbol indicating silence for a specific duration, mirroring note values.

Filled head with single tail/flag; lasts half a beat in 4/4.
